+    """Gathering WRs, WRs per chain and QPs used for `rows` rows of one
+    gatherer, chained as `proxy.chain_length` says."""
+    num_wrs = tl.cdiv(rows, ROWS_PER_WR)
+    chain = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(tl.cdiv(num_wrs, QPS), MIN_CHAIN), MAX_CHAIN)
+    return num_wrs, chain, tl.minimum(tl.cdiv(num_wrs, chain), QPS)
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["num_items"])
+def _plan_kernel(
+    ids,
+    meta,
+    counts,
+    owner_pos,
+    remote_addr,
+    keys,
+    num_items,
+    world,
+    ticket,
+    starts,
+    wr_starts,
+    wr_counts,
+    used,
+    TABLES: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    WORDS: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS_PER_WR: tl.constexpr,
+    QPS: tl.constexpr,
+    VG_P2: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Number live rows within their (table, gatherer) group into `owner_pos`
+    (-1 if dead); the last program lays out each group's slots, WRs and QPs."""
+    peers = tl.arange(0, VG_P2)
+    item = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    valid = item < num_items
+    index, table, owner, local, live = locate(ids, meta, item, valid, TABLES, K)
+    gatherers = tl.load(table + GATHERERS, mask=live, other=0)
+    gatherers = gatherers.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int32))
+    gatherer = tl.load(gatherers + owner, mask=live, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+    gatherer += index * world
+    # Positions: ranks within the block, after one atomic per group.
+    mine = ((gatherer[:, None] == peers[None, :]) & live[:, None]).to(tl.int32)
+    sizes = tl.sum(mine, 0)
+    base = tl.atomic_add(counts + peers, sizes, mask=sizes > 0)
+    before = tl.cumsum(mine, 0) - mine + base[None, :]
+    position = tl.sum(tl.where(mine > 0, before, 0), 1).to(tl.int64)
+    tl.store(
+        owner_pos + item, tl.where(live, gatherer << 32 | position, -1), mask=valid
+    )
+    bases = tl.load(table + SHARD_BASES, mask=live, other=0)
+    bases = bases.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64))
+    base_at = tl.load(bases + owner, mask=live, other=0)
+    tl.store(remote_addr + item, base_at + local * (WORDS * 8), mask=live)
+    lkeys = tl.load(table + SHARD_KEYS, mask=live, other=0)
+    lkey = tl.load(lkeys.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int32)) + owner, mask=live)
+    tl.store(keys + item, lkey, mask=live)
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    if _last_program(ticket):
+        in_vg = peers < world * TABLES
+        group_rows = tl.load(counts + peers, mask=in_vg, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+        group_wrs, _, group_qps = _wr_layout(group_rows, ROWS_PER_WR, QPS)
+        all_wrs = group_wrs + 2 * group_qps
+        tl.store(starts + peers, tl.cumsum(group_rows, 0) - group_rows, mask=in_vg)
+        tl.store(wr_starts + peers, tl.cumsum(all_wrs, 0) - all_wrs, mask=in_vg)
+        tl.store(wr_counts + peers, group_wrs, mask=in_vg)
+        tl.store(used + peers, group_qps, mask=in_vg)
+
+
+@triton.jit(
+    do_not_specialize=[
+        "num_items",
+        "rank",
+        "landing",
+        "landing_rkey",
+        "flags",
+        "flags_rkey",
+        "desc_lkey",
+    ]
+)
+def _wr_kernel(
+    owner_pos,
+    counts,
+    remote_addr,
+    keys,
+    boxes,
+    box_keys,
+    desc,
+    seq_ptr,
+    landing,
+    landing_rkey,
+    flags,
+    flags_rkey,
+    num_items,
+    world,
+    rank,
+    ticket,
+    starts,
+    wr_starts,
+    wr_counts,
+    used,
+    box_rkeys,
+    desc_lkey,
+    queues,
+    slots,
+    BOX_BYTES: tl.constexpr,
+    MAX_WRS: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS_PER_WR: tl.constexpr,
+    QPS: tl.constexpr,
+    VG_P2: tl.constexpr,
+    WORDS: tl.constexpr,
+    TABLES: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Write each group's gathering WRs and SGEs (in its gatherer's mailbox
+    layout) and each row's slot; the last program posts every group's request."""
+    peers = tl.arange(0, VG_P2)
+    item = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    packed = tl.load(owner_pos + item, mask=item < num_items, other=-1)
+    remote = packed >= 0
+    owner = packed >> 32
+    position = packed & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    start = tl.load(starts + owner, mask=remote, other=0)
+    wr_start = tl.load(wr_starts + owner, mask=remote, other=0)
+    size = tl.load(counts + owner, mask=remote, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+    num_wrs, chain, num_qps = _wr_layout(size, ROWS_PER_WR, QPS)
+    box = tl.load(boxes + owner % world, mask=remote, other=0)
+    box += owner // world * BOX_BYTES
+    slot = start + position
+    row = item // (TABLES * K) * K + item % K
+    at = slots + item // K % TABLES * (num_items // TABLES) + row
+    tl.store(at, tl.where(remote, slot, -1).to(tl.int32), mask=item < num_items)
+    key = tl.load(keys + item, mask=remote, other=0).to(tl.int64) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    addr = tl.load(remote_addr + item, mask=remote, other=0)[:, None]
+    word = tl.arange(0, SGE_WORDS)[None, :]
+    sge = _with_sge(0, word, 0, addr, WORDS * 8, key[:, None])
+    sge_at = desc + MAX_WRS * WR_WORDS + slot[:, None] * SGE_WORDS + word
+    tl.store(sge_at, sge, mask=remote[:, None])
+    first = remote & (position % ROWS_PER_WR == 0)
+    index = position // ROWS_PER_WR
+    last = (index % chain == chain - 1) | (index == num_wrs - 1)
+    head = index // chain
+    read_at = box + (num_wrs + 2 * (head % QPS)) * WR_BYTES
+    tail = tl.where(head + QPS >= tl.cdiv(num_wrs, chain), read_at, 0)
+    wr_at = box + index * WR_BYTES
+    sges = box + (num_wrs + 2 * num_qps) * WR_BYTES
+    wr_id = rank.to(tl.int64)
+    word = tl.arange(0, WR_WORDS)[None, :]
+    wr = _rdma_wr(
+        word,
+        wr_id,
+        tl.where(last, tail, wr_at + WR_BYTES)[:, None],
+        (sges + position * SGE_BYTES)[:, None],
+        tl.minimum(size - position, ROWS_PER_WR)[:, None],
+        _WRITE,
+        tl.where(last, _SIGNALED, 0).to(tl.int64)[:, None],
+        (landing + slot * (WORDS * 8))[:, None],
+        landing_rkey.to(tl.int64),
+    )
+    record = desc + (wr_start + index)[:, None] * WR_WORDS + word
+    tl.store(record, wr, mask=first[:, None])
+    # Row q writes QP q's READ of flag (owner, q) into the READ's data word,
+    # then the fenced inline WRITE of the next seq from the WRITE's.
+    is_flag = (remote & (position < num_qps))[:, None]
+    read = (box + (num_wrs + 2 * position) * WR_BYTES)[:, None]
+    write = read + WR_BYTES
+    lkey = tl.load(box_keys + owner % world, mask=remote, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+    flag = (flags + (owner * QPS + position) * 8)[:, None]
+    rkey = flags_rkey.to(tl.int64)
+    wr = _rdma_wr(word, wr_id, write, read + _WR_SGE * 8, 1, _READ, 0, flag, rkey)
+    wr = _with_sge(wr, word, _WR_SGE, read + _WR_DATA * 8, 8, lkey[:, None])
+    record = desc + (wr_start + num_wrs + 2 * position)[:, None] * WR_WORDS + word
+    tl.store(record, wr, mask=is_flag)
+    wr = _rdma_wr(
+        word, wr_id, 0, write + _WR_SGE * 8, 1, _WRITE, _INLINE_FENCE, flag, rkey
+    )
+    wr = _with_sge(wr, word, _WR_SGE, write + _WR_DATA * 8, 8, 0)
+    wr = tl.where(word == _WR_DATA, tl.load(seq_ptr) + 1, wr)
+    tl.store(record + WR_WORDS, wr, mask=is_flag)
+    # The NIC reads these only after the doorbell the last program rings.
+    _fence_sys()
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    if _last_program(ticket):
+        in_vg = peers < world * TABLES
+        sizes = tl.load(counts + peers, mask=in_vg, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+        all_wrs = tl.load(wr_counts + peers, mask=in_vg, other=0)
+        tl.debug_barrier()
+        tl.store(counts + peers, tl.zeros_like(peers), mask=in_vg)
+        if tl.sum(sizes) > 0:
+            # One read-modify-write, so every thread agrees on the sequence number.
+            tl.atomic_add(seq_ptr, 1)
+            _post_requests(
+                peers,
+                in_vg & (all_wrs > 0),
+                all_wrs,
+                sizes,
+                tl.load(starts + peers, mask=in_vg, other=0),
+                tl.load(wr_starts + peers, mask=in_vg, other=0),
+                all_wrs + 2 * tl.load(used + peers, mask=in_vg, other=0),
+                world,
+                boxes,
+                box_rkeys,
+                desc.to(tl.int64),
+                desc_lkey,
+                queues,
+                BOX_BYTES,
+                MAX_WRS,
+            )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _last_program(ticket):
+    """Whether this program is the last of its launch to get here."""
+    last = tl.atomic_add(ticket, 1, sem="acq_rel") == tl.num_programs(0) - 1
+    if last:
+        tl.store(ticket, 0)
+    return last
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _fence_sys():
+    tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        "membar.sys; mov.u32 $0, 0;", "=r", [], dtype=tl.int32, is_pure=False, pack=1
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _be32(x):
+    """The low 32 bits of `x`, big-endian, as stored by a little-endian GPU."""
+    x = x.to(tl.int64)
+    swapped = (x & 0xFF) << 24 | (x & 0xFF00) << 8 | (x >> 8) & 0xFF00
+    return (swapped | (x >> 24) & 0xFF).to(tl.uint32)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _with_be64(value, word, at, x):
+    """`value` (32-bit words) with big-endian `x` at word `at`."""
+    value = tl.where(word == at, _be32(x >> 32)[:, None], value)
+    return tl.where(word == at + 1, _be32(x)[:, None], value)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _with_data_seg(value, word, at, length, lkey, addr):
+    """`value` (32-bit words) with an mlx5_wqe_data_seg at word `at`."""
+    value = tl.where(word == at, _be32(length)[:, None], value)
+    value = tl.where(word == at + 1, lkey, value)
+    return _with_be64(value, word, at + 2, addr)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _post_requests(
+    vg,
+    active,
+    imm_wrs,
+    sizes,
+    group_first,
+    group_first_wr,
+    group_wrs,
+    world,
+    boxes,
+    box_rkeys,
+    desc_at,
+    desc_lkey,
+    queues,
+    BOX_BYTES: tl.constexpr,
+    MAX_WRS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Post each active group's `_RequestWQE` on its gatherer's QP and ring
+    the doorbell; `queues` rows are those `_map_queues` returns."""
+    gatherer = vg % world
+    queue = queues + gatherer * 8
+    # Each group's WQE index on its QP: after the active groups before it there.
+    other = vg[None, :]
+    same = (gatherer[:, None] == other % world) & active[None, :]
+    before = tl.sum((same & (other < vg[:, None])).to(tl.int64), 1)
+    last = active & (tl.sum((same & (other > vg[:, None])).to(tl.int32), 1) == 0)
+    index = tl.load(queue + 5, mask=active, other=0) + before
+    wqe_count = tl.load(queue + 1, mask=active, other=1)
+    qpn = tl.load(queue + 4, mask=active, other=0)
+    wqe = tl.load(queue, mask=active, other=0) + index % wqe_count * WQE_BYTES
+    box = tl.load(boxes + gatherer, mask=active, other=0) + vg // world * BOX_BYTES
+    rkey = tl.load(box_rkeys + gatherer, mask=active, other=0)
+    wrs_at = desc_at + group_first_wr * WR_BYTES
+    sges_at = desc_at + MAX_WRS * WR_BYTES + group_first * SGE_BYTES
+    # Big-endian 32-bit words; unsignaled, and imm raw, as the owner reads it.
+    word = tl.arange(0, WQE_WORDS)[None, :]
+    ctrl0 = _be32(index << 8 & 0xFFFF00 | _WRITE_IMM)[:, None]
+    ctrl1 = _be32(qpn << 8 | _WQE_SEGMENTS)[:, None]
+    imm = (imm_wrs | vg // world << 24).to(tl.uint32)[:, None]
+    value = tl.where(word == _WQE_OPCODE, ctrl0, 0)
+    value = tl.where(word == _WQE_QPN_DS, ctrl1, value)
+    value = tl.where(word == _WQE_IMM, imm, value)
+    value = _with_be64(value, word, _WQE_RADDR, box)
+    value = tl.where(word == _WQE_RKEY, _be32(rkey)[:, None], value)
+    lkey = _be32(desc_lkey)
+    value = _with_data_seg(value, word, _WQE_WRS, group_wrs * WR_BYTES, lkey, wrs_at)
+    value = _with_data_seg(value, word, _WQE_SGES, sizes * SGE_BYTES, lkey, sges_at)
+    at = wqe.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint32))[:, None] + word
+    tl.store(at, value, mask=active[:, None])
+    # The NIC reads the WQEs (host memory) once the doorbell rings, and the
+    # register is rung with the last WQE's first 8 bytes (its ctrl0, ctrl1).
+    _fence_sys()
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    record = tl.load(queue + 2, mask=last, other=0).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint32))
+    tl.store(record + 1, _be32(index + 1 & 0xFFFF), mask=last)
+    tl.store(queue + 5, index + 1, mask=last)
+    _fence_sys()
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    register = tl.load(queue + 3, mask=last, other=0)
+    ring = tl.sum(ctrl0.to(tl.uint64) | ctrl1.to(tl.uint64) << 32, 1)
+    # One doorbell at a time: stores to several registers at once can merge
+    # into one write that the NIC takes as a single doorbell.
+    for g in range(world):
+        mine = last & (gatherer == g)
+        if tl.sum(mine.to(tl.int32)) > 0:
+            door = tl.sum(tl.where(mine, register, 0)).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint64))
+            tl.store(door, tl.sum(tl.where(mine, ring, 0)), cache_modifier=".wt")
+            _fence_sys()
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["num_words", "table"])
+def _place_kernel(
+    owner_pos,
+    starts,
+    landing,
+    out,
+    num_words,
+    table,
+    ready,
+    TABLES: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    HOST: tl.constexpr,
+    WORDS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Once table `table`'s rows have landed, copy them to their places in
+    `out` (its `[..., K]` rows), zeroing dead rows; one word per lane."""
+    wait_landed(ready, table)
+    word = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    valid = word < num_words
+    row = word // WORDS
+    item = row // K * (TABLES * K) + table * K + row % K
+    packed = tl.load(owner_pos + item, mask=valid, other=-1)
+    live = packed >= 0
+    slot = tl.load(starts + (packed >> 32), mask=live, other=0) + (packed & 0xFFFFFFFF)
+    src = landing.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint64)) + slot * WORDS + word - row * WORDS
+    # NICs rewrite host landing between fetches: bypass caches there.
+    if HOST:
+        data = tl.load(src, mask=live, other=0, cache_modifier=".cv")
+    else:
+        data = tl.load(src, mask=live, other=0)
+    tl.store(out.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint64)) + word, data, mask=valid)
+
+
+class RdmaTransport:
+    """QPs to every peer's owner proxy (requests) and from this GPU's to every
+    peer's (gathers), and the buffers fetches go through."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        group,
+        host_shards: bool,
+        max_items: int,
+        max_row_bytes: int,
+        max_tables: int,
+        rdma_inflight: int,
+        thp_dir: str | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.group, self.host_shards = group, host_shards
+        self.thp_dir = thp_dir
+        self.rank, self.world = group.rank_in_group, group.world_size
+        # Rows per table in a fetch, and in all.
+        self.max_items, self.max_tables = max_items, max_tables
+        total = max_items * max_tables
+        self.node = node_id()
+        # Bound the WRITEs in flight per NIC: many QPs for few peers, few for many.
+        self.qps_per_peer = min(16, max(2, 128 // max(self.world - 1, 1)))
+        self._compiled: dict[tuple, Any] = {}
+        # Its own process, so it never waits for this one's GIL.
+        ours, theirs = socket.socketpair(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_SEQPACKET)
+        self.proc = subprocess.Popen(
+            [sys.executable, proxy.__file__, str(theirs.fileno())],
+            pass_fds=[theirs.fileno()],
+        )
+        theirs.close()
+        self.sock = ours
+        # Set once a request fails or the proxy exits, so every wait fails then:
+        # `start` reads the host copy, kernels the HBM one.
+        gpu = torch.device("cuda", torch.accelerator.current_device_index())
+        self.failed = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device="cpu", pin_memory=True)
+        self.failed_gpu = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=gpu)
+        self._fail_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(gpu)
+
+        def proxy_exited() -> None:
+            self.proc.wait()
+            self._fail()
+
+        threading.Thread(target=proxy_exited, daemon=True).start()
+        device = pick_device()
+        info = self._call(
+            "init",
+            device,
+            self.world,
+            self.rank,
+            self.qps_per_peer,
+            SQ_DEPTH,
+            rdma_inflight,
+        )
+        # This GPU posts its requests itself, on one QP per gatherer.
+        self.verbs = verbs.Device(device)
+        cq, channel = self.verbs.create_cq(self.world * REQUEST_DEPTH, wakeable=True)
+        made = [
+            self.verbs.create_qp(cq, cq, REQUEST_DEPTH, 2) for _ in range(self.world)
+        ]
+        logger.info(
+            "Engram pool RDMA proxy (pid %d) on %s, %d QPs per peer",
+            self.proc.pid,
+            info["device"],
+            self.qps_per_peer,
+        )
+        requests = [qpn for _, qpn in made]
+        everyone = self._all_gather(
+            {**info, "requests": requests, "max_items": max_items, "node": self.node}
+        )
+        # Each GPU's NIC gathers its node's host shards itself (`shard`), so
+        # no QPs connect GPUs of one node: their NICs may not reach each other,
+        # as on rail-optimized fabrics.
+        self.local_peers = {
+            peer
+            for peer, e in enumerate(everyone)
+            if host_shards and e["node"] == self.node and peer != self.rank
+        }
+        remote = [
+            (peer, e) for peer, e in enumerate(everyone) if peer not in self.local_peers
+        ]
+        # Every owner posts our WRs, so they fit every NIC and path.
+        self.max_sge = min(e["max_sge"] for e in everyone)
+        self.mtu = min(e["mtu"] for e in everyone)
+        # Per (table, gatherer): a partial WR, and a READ and a flag WR per QP.
+        rows_per_wr = self.rows_per_wr(max_row_bytes)
+        # Owners keep a mailbox per requester and table, sized for that
+        # requester's fetches (engines may batch differently, as P and D do).
+        box_sizes = [
+            proxy.mailbox_bytes(
+                triton.cdiv(e["max_items"], rows_per_wr) + 1 + 2 * self.qps_per_peer,
+                e["max_items"],
+            )
+            for e in everyone
+        ]
+        groups = self.world * max_tables
+        self.max_wrs = triton.cdiv(total, rows_per_wr) + groups * (
+            1 + 2 * self.qps_per_peer
+        )
+        try:
+            mailboxes = self._call(
+                "connect",
+                [
+                    [peer, e["address"], e["qpns"][self.rank]]
+                    for peer, e in remote
+                    if peer != self.rank
+                ],
+                [[peer, e["address"], e["requests"][self.rank]] for peer, e in remote],
+                box_sizes,
+                max_tables,
+            )
+            for peer, e in remote:
+                gid, lid = e["address"]
+                qp = made[peer][0]
+                address = (bytes.fromhex(gid), lid)
+                self.verbs.connect(qp, e["notices"][self.rank], address)
+        except RuntimeError as err:
+            near = [p for p, e in remote if e["node"] == self.node and p != self.rank]
+            if not near:
+                raise
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Engram pool RDMA could not connect GPU {self.rank}'s NIC to its "
+                f"node's GPUs {near}. If the NICs of a node cannot reach each "
+                "other (as on rail-optimized fabrics), use host shards "
+                "(cpu_offload): they need no connections within a node."
+            ) from err
+        peers = {qpn: peer for peer, (_, qpn) in enumerate(made)}
+        threading.Thread(
+            target=self._watch, args=(cq, channel, peers), daemon=True
+        ).start()
+        from cuda.bindings import driver as cu
+
+        _, ordering = cu.cuDeviceGetAttribute(
+            cu.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING,
+            cu.cuDeviceGet(gpu.index)[1],
+        )
+        # Rows, and the flags behind them, land in HBM if this GPU sees the
+        # NIC's writes there in order without a flush; else in host memory.
+        landing_bytes = total * max_row_bytes

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""How kernels find rows: which GPU owns an id (transports), and where a
+fetched row is once it has landed (`landed_row`, for models' kernels)."""
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+# A table's int64 `meta` words: its split, then device arrays per shard.
+ROWS_PER_SHARD: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(0)
+NUM_ROWS: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(1)
+SHARD_BASES: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(2)
+SHARD_KEYS: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(3)
+GATHERERS: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(4)
+META_WORDS: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(5)
+
+# An RDMA fetch's `ready` words.
+READY_SEQ: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(0)
+READY_USED: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(1)
+READY_FLAGS: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(2)
+READY_WORLD: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(3)
+READY_QPS: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(4)
+READY_TIMEOUT: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(5)
+READY_LANDED: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(6)
+READY_FAILED: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(7)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def locate(ids, meta, item, valid, TABLES: tl.constexpr, K: tl.constexpr):
+    """Item `item` of `[..., TABLES, K]` ids: its table index and `meta` row,
+    the owner GPU of its row and the row's index there, and whether it is live."""
+    index = item // K % TABLES
+    table = meta + index * META_WORDS
+    row = tl.load(ids + item, mask=valid, other=-1).to(tl.int64)
+    rows_per_shard = tl.load(table + ROWS_PER_SHARD, mask=valid, other=1)
+    num_rows = tl.load(table + NUM_ROWS, mask=valid, other=0)
+    live = valid & (row >= 0) & (row < num_rows)
+    owner = tl.where(live, row // rows_per_shard, 0)
+    return index, table, owner, row - owner * rows_per_shard, live
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def wait_landed(ready, table):
+    """Spin until every QP that gathered rows of `table` in the fetch `ready`
+    describes has flagged them landed; trap after the timeout."""
+    seq = tl.load(tl.load(ready + READY_SEQ).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)))
+    # The first program to see every flag records `seq` here for the others.
+    landed = tl.load(ready + READY_LANDED).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) + table
+    waiting = 0
+    # Acquire: rows are read only after the word that says they landed.
+    mark = tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        "ld.acquire.gpu.global.b64 $0, [$1];",
+        "=l,l",
+        [landed.to(tl.int64)],
+        dtype=tl.int64,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+    if mark != seq:
+        used = tl.load(ready + READY_USED).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int32))
+        flags = tl.load(ready + READY_FLAGS).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64))
+        world, qps = tl.load(ready + READY_WORLD), tl.load(ready + READY_QPS)
+        deadline = tl.extra.cuda.globaltimer() + tl.load(ready + READY_TIMEOUT)
+        # Set by the host once a request failed or the proxy exited.
+        failed = tl.load(ready + READY_FAILED).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64))
+        q = tl.arange(0, 16)[None, :]
+        # Eight gatherers' flags (QPs per peer <= 16) per load.
+        for first in range(0, world, 8):
+            peer = first + tl.arange(0, 8)
+            group = table * world + peer
+            count = tl.load(used + group, mask=peer < world, other=0)
+            at = flags + group[:, None] * qps + q
+            waiting = 1
+            while (
+                (waiting > 0)
+                & (tl.extra.cuda.globaltimer() < deadline)
+                & (tl.load(failed, volatile=True) == 0)
+            ):
+                flag = tl.load(at, mask=q < count[:, None], other=seq, volatile=True)
+                waiting = tl.sum(tl.sum((flag != seq).to(tl.int32), 1))
+        if waiting == 0:
+            tl.atomic_xchg(landed, seq, sem="release")
+    if waiting > 0:
+        tl.device_print("Engram pool RDMA fetch failed (see log) or timed out", seq)
+        tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+            "trap;", "=r", [], dtype=tl.int32, is_pure=False, pack=1
+        )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def landed_row(
+    rows,
+    slots,
+    ready,
+    table,
+    row,
+    valid,
+    ROW_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    PLACED: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Address of fetched row `row` of `table` (args from `EngramFetch.landed`),
+    and whether it holds data (else load zeros). Call from every program."""
+    slot, live = row, valid
+    if not PLACED:
+        wait_landed(ready, table)
+        slot = tl.load(slots + row, mask=valid, other=-1).to(tl.int64)
+        live = valid & (slot >= 0)
+    return rows + tl.multiple_of(slot * ROW_STRIDE, ROW_STRIDE & -ROW_STRIDE), live

+"""DSv4.1 Engram tables in an Engram pool (`vllm.distributed.engram_pool`): pool
+rows hold values then E8M0 scales; layers unpack MXFP8 WKV input as rows land."""
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm.config import get_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.distributed import get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size
+from vllm.distributed.engram_pool import (
+    EngramFetch,
+    EngramPool,
+    EngramPrefetch,
+    get_engram_pool,
+    landed_row,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fusion.quant_activation import QuantizedActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.utils import set_weight_attrs
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.engram import (
+    Engram,
+    EngramBatch,
+    EngramLayout,
+    ParallelEngramEmbedding,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.query_quant import (
+    can_fuse_query_quant,
+    mxfp8_scale_bytes,
+    mxfp8_scale_offset,
+)
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+# Values per E8M0 scale.
+SCALE_BLOCK = 32
+_SCALE: tl.constexpr = tl.constexpr(SCALE_BLOCK)
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["num_rows"])
+def _dequant_rows_kernel(
+    packed,
+    out,
+    num_rows,
+    ROW_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    PACKED_FP4: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Dequantize pool rows (FP8 or MXFP4 values, then E8M0 scales) into BF16."""
+    rows = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    valid = rows < num_rows
+    ROW_BYTES: tl.constexpr = DIM // 2 if PACKED_FP4 else DIM
+    src = packed + rows * ROW_STRIDE
+    cols = tl.arange(0, DIM)
+    if PACKED_FP4:
+        byte = tl.load(
+            src[:, None] + (cols // 2)[None, :], mask=valid[:, None], other=0
+        ).to(tl.int32)
+        nib = tl.where(cols[None, :] % 2 == 0, byte & 0xF, (byte >> 4) & 0xF)
+        e = (nib & 0x7) >> 1
+        m = (nib & 0x1).to(tl.float32)
+        pow2 = ((e - 2 + 127) << 23).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
+        mag = tl.where(e == 0, m * 0.5, (2.0 + m) * pow2)
+        values = tl.where((nib & 0x8) != 0, -mag, mag)
+    else:
+        values = tl.load(
+            src.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.float8e4nv))[:, None] + cols[None, :],
+            mask=valid[:, None],
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+    scale = tl.load(
+        src[:, None] + ROW_BYTES + (cols // _SCALE)[None, :],
+        mask=valid[:, None],
+        other=0,
+    )
+    scale = (scale.to(tl.int32) << 23).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
+    tl.store(
+        out + rows[:, None] * DIM + cols[None, :],
+        (values * scale).to(tl.bfloat16),
+        mask=valid[:, None],
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["num_tokens", "table"])
+def _unpack_fp8_kernel(
+    rows,
+    slots,
+    ready,
+    values,
+    scales,
+    num_tokens,
+    table,
+    HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    ROW_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    PLACED: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Split table `table`'s fetched `[token][head]` rows into MXFP8 values and
+    F8_128x4 scales; scales past `num_tokens` zero-pad the 128-row tile."""
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    token, head = row // HEADS, row % HEADS
+    valid = token < num_tokens
+    src, live = landed_row(rows, slots, ready, table, row, valid, ROW_STRIDE, PLACED)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, DIM)
+    data = tl.load(src[:, None] + cols[None, :], mask=live[:, None], other=0)
+    tl.store(values + row[:, None] * DIM + cols[None, :], data, mask=valid[:, None])
+    scale_cols = tl.arange(0, DIM // _SCALE)
+    scale = tl.load(
+        src[:, None] + DIM + scale_cols[None, :], mask=live[:, None], other=0
+    )
+    group = head[:, None] * (DIM // _SCALE) + scale_cols[None, :]
+    offset = mxfp8_scale_offset(token[:, None], group, HEADS * DIM // _SCALE)

+class PoolEngramEmbedding(ParallelEngramEmbedding):
+    """A table whose rows an Engram pool splits over GPUs of several engines;
+    its parameters are views of this GPU's shard, so loaders fill it in place."""

+    def __init__(

+        self.row_bytes = dim // 2 if packed_fp4 else dim
+        self.n_hash_cols = self.part_n_hash_cols = len(head_sizes)
+        self.tp_size = self.dp_size = 1
+        self.cpu_offload = False
+        self.pool = pool
+        weight_dtype = torch.uint8 if packed_fp4 else torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        scale_dim = dim // SCALE_BLOCK
+        if torch.get_default_device().type == "meta":

+            row_start = 0
+            weight = torch.empty(sum(head_sizes), self.row_bytes, dtype=weight_dtype)
+            scales = torch.empty(sum(head_sizes), scale_dim, dtype=torch.uint8)

+            scales = shard[:, self.row_bytes :]

+            )

+        set_weight_attrs(self.weight, {"dummy_weight_value": 1.0})
+        set_weight_attrs(self.weight_scale_inv, {"dummy_weight_value": 127})

+        assert self.table is not None
+        shard = self.table.shard.data_ptr()
+        if (self.weight.data_ptr(), self.weight_scale_inv.data_ptr()) != (
+            shard,
+            shard + self.row_bytes,
+        ):

+    def lookup(
+        self, indices: torch.Tensor, out: torch.Tensor, background: bool = False
+    ) -> None:
+        """Look up every head of `indices` into BF16 `out`."""
+        assert self.table is not None and out.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        rows = indices.shape[0] * self.n_hash_cols

+        _dequant_rows_kernel[(triton.cdiv(rows, 16),)](
+            packed,
+            out,
+            rows,
+            ROW_STRIDE=self.table.row_stride,
+            DIM=self.dim,
+            PACKED_FP4=self.packed_fp4,
+            BLOCK=16,
+        )
+
+
+class PoolEngram(Engram):
+    """An Engram layer whose table is split over an Engram pool."""
+
+    def _create_embedding(
+        self, layout: EngramLayout, layer_hash_index: int
+    ) -> ParallelEngramEmbedding:
+        # One fetch reads every Engram layer's table.
+        n_hash_cols = (layout.max_ngram_size - 1) * layout.n_heads
+        max_tokens = get_current_vllm_config().scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens
+        pool = get_engram_pool(
+            max_tokens * n_hash_cols,
+            layout.row_bytes + layout.head_dim // SCALE_BLOCK,
+            len(layout.num_embeddings),

+            layout.num_embeddings[layer_hash_index],
+            layout.head_dim,
+            tuple(size for order in layout.primes[layer_hash_index] for size in order),
+            layout.packed_fp4,
+            pool,
+            f"layer{layout.layer_ids[layer_hash_index]}",
+        )
+
+

+    """Stage every layer's MXFP8 WKV input from one pool fetch per step: each
+    layer's rows are unpacked as they land (`EngramPrefetch`)."""

+    def __init__(self, layers: list[Engram], max_tokens: int) -> None:

+        self.fp8_scales = torch.empty(
+            len(layers),
+            mxfp8_scale_bytes(max_tokens, width),
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        tables = [layer.embed_tokens.table for layer in layers]

+            layer._batch = self

+                (0, *layer.staged_rows.shape[1:])

+    @classmethod
+    def create(cls, layers: list[Engram], max_tokens: int) -> "EngramBatch | None":

+def _mxfp4(weight: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Pack E2M1 grid weights with unit E8M0 scales."""
+    magnitudes = torch.tensor((0.0, *E2M1_CODES), device=weight.device)
+    experts, rows, cols = weight.shape
+    packed = torch.empty(
+        experts, rows, cols // 2, dtype=torch.uint8, device=weight.device
+    )
+    # Bound the float32 values and int64 codes to one expert.

+        codes = torch.searchsorted(magnitudes, values)
+        assert torch.equal(magnitudes[codes], values)
+        packed[expert] = codes[:, 0::2] | (codes[:, 1::2] << 4)
+    # E8M0 127 encodes 2**0.
+    scale = torch.full(
+        (experts, rows, cols // 32), 127, dtype=torch.uint8, device=weight.device
+    )
+    return packed, scale

+  default_frontend: rust
+
+features:
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "HY4 tool call parser with automatic tool choice (also sets the paired hy_v4 reasoning parser)"
+    args:
+      - "--enable-auto-tool-choice"
+      - "--tool-call-parser"
+      - "hy_v4"
+      - "--reasoning-parser"
+      - "hy_v4"
+  reasoning:
+    description: "HY4 reasoning parser — returns the chain of thought separately from the final answer"
+    args:
+      - "--reasoning-parser"
+      - "hy_v4"
+  spec_decoding:
+    description: "DFly2 speculative decoding with the checkpoint's built-in five-layer draft (5 speculative tokens)"
+    args:
+      - "--speculative-config"
+      - '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dfly"}'
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    model_id: "tencent/Hy4-FP8"
+    precision: fp8
+    vram_minimum_gb: 944
+    description: "Block-FP8 checkpoint (tencent/Hy4-FP8), BF16 compute — 786 GB of weights"
+  bf16:
+    precision: bf16
+    vram_minimum_gb: 1859
+    description: "BF16 checkpoint (tencent/Hy4) — 1,549 GB of weights; needs an 8x B300 node"
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+
+strategy_overrides:
+  single_node_tp:
+    tp: 8
+
+notes:
+  - title: "Host memory for the BF16 checkpoint"
+    when: { variants: [bf16] }
+    body: |
+      The BF16 checkpoint is 1,549 GB across 245 shards. Provision host RAM and
+      page cache for loading it; the evaluation host had 2 TiB.
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  HY4 is the Tencent Hy Team's flagship Mixture-of-Experts model for text and
+  image understanding, with up to 1M tokens of context. Two checkpoints share
+  one architecture (`HYV4VLForConditionalGeneration`):
+
+  - [HY4 FP8](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-FP8) — the default variant,
+    and the checkpoint the model card serves
+  - [HY4 BF16](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4) — the BF16 variant
+
+  The language backbone has 770B parameters, 49B of them active per token,
+  across 78 layers. The first layer has a dense FFN; the other 77 use 256
+  routed experts (top-8) and one shared expert. Attention is gated sparse MLA
+  with cross-layer index reuse, and iHC connects the residual streams. A
+  40-layer vision encoder (1.23B) and the five-layer DFly2 draft (3.3B) bring
+  the stored total to about 774B.
+
+  HY4 is not [HY4 Flash](https://recipes.vllm.ai/tencent/Hy4-flash) or the
+  text-only [Hy4-preview](https://recipes.vllm.ai/tencent/Hy4-preview). Those
+  are separate checkpoints with their own recipes.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - **Hardware**: one 8-GPU NVIDIA node. FP8 needs about 944 GB of aggregate GPU
+    memory and BF16 about 1,859 GB (8x B300). AMD Instinct is not supported:
+    vLLM's ROCm port has neither the vision encoder nor the DFly2 drafter.
+  - **vLLM**: the `vllm/vllm-openai:hy4` image, or a nightly wheel. v0.34.0
+    does not register the architecture; 0.35.0 will be the first release
+    with it.
+  - **Host memory**: enough RAM to load the checkpoint — 786 GB (FP8) or
+    1,549 GB (BF16) on disk, 245 safetensors shards each.
+
+  ## Serving configuration
+
+  The defaults follow the model card's launch line: FP8 checkpoint, TP8, Rust
+  frontend, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` attention, BF16 compute, tool calling, reasoning
+  parsing, and DFly2 with five speculative tokens.
+
+  - **Parsers**: HY4 pairs its tool-call and reasoning parsers (`hy_v4`). Tool
+    calling sets both and adds automatic tool choice.
+  - **DFly2**: the draft ships inside both checkpoints and shares the target's
+    KV cache and sparse indices, so it needs no extra checkpoint or KV memory.
+    It requires data, pipeline, prefill-context and decode-context parallel
+    sizes of 1, which is why the recipe offers single-node TP only. The
+    checkpoints have no MTP layers (`num_nextn_predict_layers=0`), so `mtp`
+    is not an alternative method.
+  - **FP8**: blockwise W8A8 compressed-tensors quantization; `lm_head`, the
+    vision tower, the first layer's attention and the indexer projections stay
+    unquantized. vLLM reads the scheme from the checkpoint, so no quantization
+    flag is needed. It is not the MXFP8 format of Hy4-preview-FP8.
+  - **Multimodal**: one image per prompt, video off, as on the model card.
+    Raise `--limit-mm-per-prompt` to allow more.
+
+  ## Context and capacity
+
+  The checkpoints advertise 1,048,576 positions. The recipe starts from the
+  evaluated window: 131,072 tokens, 32 concurrent sequences and 8,192 batched
+  tokens. The model card's launch line sets none of the three, which serves the
+  full 1M window; raise them to match your memory budget. A full 1M-token
+  request has not been validated for this recipe.
+
+  ## Client usage
+
+  The model name is the selected checkpoint ID: `tencent/Hy4-FP8` by default,
+  `tencent/Hy4` for the BF16 variant. Tencent recommends `temperature=0.9` and
+  `top_p=1.0`.
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="tencent/Hy4-FP8",
+      messages=[{
+          "role": "user",
+          "content": [
+              {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/chart.png"}},
+              {"type": "text", "text": "Summarize this chart."},
+          ],
+      }],
+      temperature=0.9,
+      top_p=1.0,
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.reasoning)  # chain of thought
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)    # final answer
+  ```
+
+  `reasoning_effort` accepts `high` (the default, for math, coding and other
+  complex tasks) and `no_think` for a direct answer:
+
+  ```python
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="tencent/Hy4-FP8",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 multiplied by 23?"}],
+      temperature=0.9,
+      top_p=1.0,
+      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "no_think"}},
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [HY4 research page](https://hy.tencent.ai/research/hy4)
+  - [BF16 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4)
+  - [FP8 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-FP8)
+  - [GitHub: Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4)
+  - [AngelSpec, the DFly2 training toolkit](https://github.com/Tencent/AngelSpec)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Correctness tests for the RDNA3/RDNA3.5 (gfx11) int4 x int8 MoE decode kernel.
+
+`moe_w4a8_decode_rdna3` consumes the TritonWNA16Experts weight tensors
+(uint8 codes, optional nibble-packed zero points) and quantizes activations
+to int8 per 32 values. It is checked against:
+  - a torch reference that applies the same activation quantization
+    (tight tolerance), and
+  - the Triton WNA16 `fused_experts` path on the same tensors (loose
+    tolerance, int8 activation error only), which also pins the layout.
+
+Run `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_moe_int4_int8.py`.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    pytest.skip("RDNA3 int4 x int8 MoE kernel is ROCm-only", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from tests.kernels.moe.utils import make_dummy_moe_config  # noqa: E402
+from vllm import _custom_ops as ops  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import (  # noqa: E402
+    MoEActivation,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (  # noqa: E402
+    int4_w4a16_moe_quant_config,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.rdna3_int4_int8_moe import (  # noqa: E402, E501
+    RDNA3_INT4_INT8_MAX_TOKENS,
+    Rdna3Int4Int8Experts,
+    moe_w4a8_workspace_bytes,
+    rdna3_int4_int8_moe_kernel_available,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.triton_moe import (  # noqa: E402
+    TritonWNA16Experts,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe import (  # noqa: E402
+    fused_experts,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not rdna3_int4_int8_moe_kernel_available(),
+    reason="Requires a gfx11 GPU and the moe_w4a8_decode_rdna3 op",
+)
+
+device = "cuda"
+
+# (E, K=hidden, N=intermediate, top_k, group_size). E is capped; the kernel
+# is expert-count independent.
+SHAPES = [
+    pytest.param(16, 2048, 512, 8, 128, id="qwen3.6-35b-a3b-g128"),
+    pytest.param(16, 2048, 768, 8, 32, id="qwen3-30b-a3b-g32"),
+    pytest.param(8, 256, 128, 2, 64, id="small-g64"),
+]
+NUM_TOKENS = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64]
+
+
+def _pack_k(codes: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[..., K] codes in [0, 16) -> [..., K/2] uint8, low nibble = even k."""
+    return codes[..., 0::2] | (codes[..., 1::2] << 4)
+
+
+def _pack_rows(zp: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[E, R, G] zero points -> [E, R/2, G] uint8, low nibble = even row."""
+    return zp[:, 0::2] | (zp[:, 1::2] << 4)
+
+
+def _make_expert_weights(E, rows, cols, group, dtype, with_zp, gen):
+    codes = torch.randint(
+        0, 16, (E, rows, cols), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device, generator=gen
+    )
+    scale = (
+        torch.rand((E, rows, cols // group), device=device, generator=gen) * 0.02
+        + 0.005
+    ).to(dtype)
+    if with_zp:
+        zp = torch.randint(
+            0,
+            16,
+            (E, rows, cols // group),
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            device=device,
+            generator=gen,
+        )
+    else:
+        zp = torch.full((E, rows, cols // group), 8, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+    deq = (
+        codes.float() - zp.repeat_interleave(group, -1).float()
+    ) * scale.float().repeat_interleave(group, -1)
+    packed_zp = _pack_rows(zp) if with_zp else None
+    return _pack_k(codes), scale, packed_zp, deq
+
+
+def _quant_act_ref(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Symmetric int8 fake-quant per 32 values, as the kernel does."""
+    shape = x.shape
+    g = x.reshape(*shape[:-1], shape[-1] // 32, 32)
+    scale = (g.abs().amax(-1, keepdim=True) / 127.0).clamp_min(1e-12)
+    q = torch.round(g / scale).clamp(-127, 127)
+    return (q * scale).reshape(shape)
+
+
+def _reference(x, topk_ids, topk_w, w13_deq, w2_deq, quant_act=True):
+    E, two_n, _ = w13_deq.shape
+    N = two_n // 2
+    xf = x.float()
+    xq = _quant_act_ref(xf) if quant_act else xf
+    out = torch.zeros(x.size(0), w2_deq.size(1), device=device)
+    for m in range(x.size(0)):
+        for s in range(topk_ids.size(1)):
+            e = int(topk_ids[m, s])
+            if e < 0 or e >= E:
+                continue
+            gu = w13_deq[e] @ xq[m]
+            h = F.silu(gu[:N]) * gu[N:]
+            hq = _quant_act_ref(h) if quant_act else h
+            out[m] += topk_w[m, s] * (w2_deq[e] @ hq)
+    return out
+
+
+def _routing(M, E, top_k, gen):
+    ids = torch.stack(
+        [torch.randperm(E, device=device, generator=gen)[:top_k] for _ in range(M)]
+    ).to(torch.int32)
+    logits = torch.randn(M, top_k, device=device, generator=gen)
+    return ids, torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
+
+
+def _rel_err(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    return ((a.float() - b.float()).norm() / b.float().norm().clamp_min(1e-12)).item()
+
+
+def _setup(E, K, N, top_k, group, dtype, with_zp, M, seed=0):
+    gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
+    w13, w13_s, w13_zp, w13_deq = _make_expert_weights(
+        E, 2 * N, K, group, dtype, with_zp, gen
+    )
+    w2, w2_s, w2_zp, w2_deq = _make_expert_weights(E, K, N, group, dtype, with_zp, gen)
+    x = torch.randn(M, K, device=device, generator=gen).to(dtype)
+    ids, wts = _routing(M, E, top_k, gen)
+    return x, ids, wts, (w13, w13_s, w13_zp, w2, w2_s, w2_zp), (w13_deq, w2_deq)
+
+
+def _workspace(M, K, N, top_k):
+    nbytes = moe_w4a8_workspace_bytes(M, K, N, top_k)
+    return torch.empty(nbytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+
+
+def _run(x, ids, wts, w, expert_map=None, workspace=None):
+    out = torch.empty_like(x)
+    w13 = w[0]
+    if workspace is None:
+        workspace = _workspace(x.size(0), x.size(1), w13.size(1) // 2, ids.size(1))
+    ops.moe_w4a8_decode_rdna3(out, x, ids, wts, expert_map, workspace, *w)
+    return out
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("E,K,N,top_k,group", SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("M", NUM_TOKENS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_zp", [False, True])
+def test_matches_w4a8_reference(E, K, N, top_k, group, M, dtype, with_zp):
+    x, ids, wts, w, deq = _setup(E, K, N, top_k, group, dtype, with_zp, M)
+    out = _run(x, ids, wts, w)
+    ref = _reference(x, ids, wts, *deq)
+    assert _rel_err(out, ref) < 1e-2
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("E,K,N,top_k,group", SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("M", [1, 8, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_zp", [False, True])
+def test_close_to_triton_wna16(E, K, N, top_k, group, M, with_zp):
+    """Same weight tensors through the Triton W4A16 path."""
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    x, ids, wts, w, _ = _setup(E, K, N, top_k, group, dtype, with_zp, M)
+    w13, w13_s, w13_zp, w2, w2_s, w2_zp = w
+    out = _run(x, ids, wts, w)
+    quant_config = int4_w4a16_moe_quant_config(
+        w1_scale=w13_s,
+        w2_scale=w2_s,
+        w1_zp=w13_zp,
+        w2_zp=w2_zp,
+        block_shape=[0, group],
+    )
+    ref = fused_experts(x, w13, w2, wts, ids, quant_config=quant_config)
+    assert _rel_err(out, ref) < 5e-2
+
+
+def test_masked_slots_are_skipped():
+    E, K, N, top_k, group = 8, 256, 128, 4, 64
+    x, ids, wts, w, deq = _setup(E, K, N, top_k, group, torch.bfloat16, True, 4)
+    ids[0, 1] = -1
+    ids[2, :] = -1
+    ids[3, 3] = E
+    out = _run(x, ids, wts, w)
+    ref = _reference(x, ids, wts, *deq)
+    assert torch.all(out[2] == 0)
+    assert _rel_err(out, ref) < 1e-2
+
+
+def test_repeated_expert_and_zero_input():
+    E, K, N, top_k, group = 8, 256, 128, 4, 64
+    x, ids, wts, w, deq = _setup(E, K, N, top_k, group, torch.bfloat16, False, 2)
+    ids[:] = 3
+    out = _run(x, ids, wts, w)
+    assert _rel_err(out, _reference(x, ids, wts, *deq)) < 1e-2
+
+    zero = torch.zeros_like(x)
+    assert torch.all(_run(zero, ids, wts, w) == 0)
+
+
+def test_deterministic():
+    x, ids, wts, w, _ = _setup(16, 2048, 512, 8, 128, torch.bfloat16, False, 4)
+    first = _run(x, ids, wts, w)
+    for _ in range(3):
+        assert torch.equal(_run(x, ids, wts, w), first)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ids_dtype", [torch.int32, torch.int64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("wts_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_routing_dtypes(ids_dtype, wts_dtype):
+    """topk_ids and topk_weights are read in the router's dtypes."""

+    wts = wts.to(wts_dtype)
+    out = _run(x, ids.to(ids_dtype), wts, w)

+    assert _rel_err(out, _reference(x, ids, wts.float(), *deq)) < 1e-2
+
+
+def test_expert_map():
+    """Global ids go through expert_map; experts of other ranks (-1) are
+    skipped."""
+    E_global, K, N, top_k, group = 16, 256, 128, 4, 64

+    local = torch.arange(E_global, device=device) % 2 == 0  # this rank: even ids
+    expert_map = torch.full((E_global,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)

+
+def test_workspace_too_small_is_rejected():

+
+def _experts(cls, E, K, N, top_k, w, num_experts=None):
+    w13, w13_s, w13_zp, w2, w2_s, w2_zp = w
+    moe_config = make_dummy_moe_config(
+        num_experts=num_experts or E,
+        num_local_experts=E,
+        experts_per_token=top_k,
+        hidden_dim=K,
+        intermediate_size=N,
+        in_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+    )
+    quant_config = int4_w4a16_moe_quant_config(
+        w1_scale=w13_s,
+        w2_scale=w2_s,
+        w1_zp=w13_zp,
+        w2_zp=w2_zp,
+        block_shape=[0, K // w13_s.size(2)],
+    )
+    return cls(moe_config, quant_config)
+
+
+def _apply(experts, x, w, ids, wts, expert_map=None, global_num_experts=-1):
+    w13, w2 = w[0], w[3]
+    M, K = x.shape
+    ws13_shape, ws2_shape, out_shape = experts.workspace_shapes(
+        M, w13.size(1), K, ids.size(1), global_num_experts, w13.size(0), None,
+        MoEActivation.SILU,
+    )  # fmt: skip
+    ws13 = torch.empty(ws13_shape, dtype=x.dtype, device=device)
+    ws2 = torch.empty(ws2_shape, dtype=x.dtype, device=device)
+    out = torch.zeros(out_shape, dtype=x.dtype, device=device)
+    experts.apply(
+        out, x, w13, w2, wts, ids, MoEActivation.SILU, global_num_experts,
+        expert_map, None, None, ws13, ws2, None, False,
+    )  # fmt: skip
+    return out
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Int4-weight, int8-activation MoE decode experts for RDNA3/RDNA3.5 (gfx11).
+
+For small batches, `moe_w4a8_decode_rdna3` replaces the two Triton WNA16
+GEMMs, the activation and the top-k reduction with three HIP launches.
+Activations and the SiLU-and-mul output are quantized to int8 per 32 values
+(`kInt8Dynamic32Sym`) and reduced with `v_dot4_i32_iu8`. The experts are
+selected for that activation key, i.e. with
+`--quantization-config.moe.activation int8_per_group_32`, or with
+`--moe-backend rdna3_int4_int8`.
+
+Weights stay in the `TritonWNA16Experts` format (uint8, two codes per byte,
+optional nibble-packed zero points), so larger batches and unsupported
+configurations fall back to the Triton kernels on the same tensors. A request
+therefore decodes with int8 activations while the batch has at most
+`RDNA3_INT4_INT8_MAX_TOKENS` tokens and with fp16/bf16 activations above that.
+"""
+
+from math import prod
+
+import torch
+
+import vllm._custom_ops as ops
+import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.modular_kernel as mk
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.triton_moe import (
+    TritonWNA16Experts,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
+    QuantKey,
+    kInt4Static,
+    kInt4Static32,
+    kInt4Static32Asym,
+    kInt4StaticAsym,
+    kInt8Dynamic32Sym,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+# Per-layer sweep on gfx1151 (eager, weights not in cache, M = 1..64) on the
+# Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MoE shapes: the decode kernel is
+# faster than the Triton WNA16 GEMMs at every M measured, 1.1-1.3x on
+# Flash-Next and 2.0-7.5x on Qwen3.6. Not measured above 64; larger steps
+# (prefill chunks, more than 64 decoding requests) use the Triton kernels.
+RDNA3_INT4_INT8_MAX_TOKENS = 64
+
+
+def _align16(nbytes: int) -> int:
+    return (nbytes + 15) // 16 * 16
+
+
+def moe_w4a8_workspace_bytes(M: int, K: int, N: int, top_k: int) -> int:
+    """Scratch bytes `moe_w4a8_decode_rdna3` carves from its workspace: int8
+    activations with fp32 scales and int32 sums per 32 values, for the input
+    [M, K] and the activation output [M * top_k, N] (N = intermediate size).
+    Mirrors `workspace_bytes` in csrc/rocm/moe_w4a8_decode_rdna3.cu."""
+    rows = M * top_k
+    return (
+        _align16(M * K)
+        + 2 * _align16(M * (K // 32) * 4)
+        + _align16(rows * N)
+        + 2 * _align16(rows * (N // 32) * 4)
+    )
+
+
+def rdna3_int4_int8_moe_kernel_available() -> bool:
+    """Whether the int4 x int8 MoE decode kernel is built and the GPU is gfx11."""
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx11
+
+    return (
+        on_gfx11()
+        and hasattr(torch.ops, "_rocm_C")
+        and hasattr(torch.ops._rocm_C, "moe_w4a8_decode_rdna3")
+    )
+
+
+class Rdna3Int4Int8Experts(TritonWNA16Experts):
+    """Triton WNA16 experts with an int4 x int8 HIP decode path on gfx11."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_current_device() -> bool:
+        return rdna3_int4_int8_moe_kernel_available()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def executed_activation_key(
+        weight_key: QuantKey | None,
+        activation_key: QuantKey | None,
+    ) -> QuantKey | None:
+        # Not weight-only like the Triton parent: the decode kernel quantizes
+        # activations itself, to the one key `_supports_quant_scheme` accepts.
+        return activation_key
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_quant_scheme(
+        weight_key: QuantKey | None,
+        activation_key: QuantKey | None,
+    ) -> bool:
+        return activation_key == kInt8Dynamic32Sym and weight_key in (
+            kInt4Static,
+            kInt4StaticAsym,
+            kInt4Static32,
+            kInt4Static32Asym,
+        )
+
+    def _use_decode_kernel(
+        self,
+        output: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        w1: torch.Tensor,
+        w2: torch.Tensor,
+        activation: MoEActivation,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,
+    ) -> bool:
+        if hidden_states.size(0) > RDNA3_INT4_INT8_MAX_TOKENS:
+            return False
+        if activation != MoEActivation.SILU:
+            return False
+        if self.activation_config.clamp_limit is not None:
+            return False
+        if apply_router_weight_on_input or self._lora_context is not None:
+            return False
+        # The kernel weights and reduces the top-k rows itself.
+        if self._uses_post_gemm2_hook(hidden_states.size(0)):
+            return False
+        if self.w1_bias is not None or self.w2_bias is not None:
+            return False
+        if hidden_states.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            return False
+        if self.w1_scale is None or self.w2_scale is None:
+            return False
+        if self.w1_scale.dtype != hidden_states.dtype:
+            return False
+        if not (hidden_states.is_contiguous() and output.is_contiguous()):
+            return False
+        # Hidden size, intermediate size and both group sizes must be
+        # multiples of 32 (one int8 activation group).
+        K = hidden_states.size(1)
+        N = w2.size(2) * 2
+        groups1 = self.w1_scale.size(2)
+        groups2 = self.w2_scale.size(2)
+        return (
+            K % 32 == 0
+            and N % 32 == 0
+            and K % groups1 == 0
+            and (K // groups1) % 32 == 0
+            and N % groups2 == 0
+            and (N // groups2) % 32 == 0
+        )
+
+    def workspace_shapes(
+        self,
+        M: int,
+        N: int,
+        K: int,
+        topk: int,
+        global_num_experts: int,
+        local_num_experts: int,
+        expert_tokens_meta: mk.ExpertTokensMetadata | None,
+        activation: MoEActivation,
+    ) -> tuple[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]]:
+        workspace13, workspace2, output = super().workspace_shapes(
+            M,
+            N,
+            K,
+            topk,
+            global_num_experts,
+            local_num_experts,
+            expert_tokens_meta,
+            activation,
+        )
+        if M <= RDNA3_INT4_INT8_MAX_TOKENS:
+            # The decode kernel's scratch lives in workspace2, which holds
+            # fp16/bf16 elements (N is the gate_up width, 2x intermediate).
+            needed = -(-moe_w4a8_workspace_bytes(M, K, N // 2, topk) // 2)
+            if needed > prod(workspace2):
+                workspace2 = (needed,)
+        return workspace13, workspace2, output
+
+    def apply(
+        self,
+        output: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        w1: torch.Tensor,
+        w2: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        activation: MoEActivation,
+        global_num_experts: int,
+        expert_map: torch.Tensor | None,
+        a1q_scale: torch.Tensor | None,
+        a2_scale: torch.Tensor | None,
+        workspace13: torch.Tensor,
+        workspace2: torch.Tensor,
+        expert_tokens_meta: mk.ExpertTokensMetadata | None,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,
+    ):
+        if not self._use_decode_kernel(
+            output, hidden_states, w1, w2, activation, apply_router_weight_on_input
+        ):
+            super().apply(
+                output,
+                hidden_states,
+                w1,
+                w2,
+                topk_weights,
+                topk_ids,
+                activation,
+                global_num_experts,
+                expert_map,
+                a1q_scale,
+                a2_scale,
+                workspace13,
+                workspace2,
+                expert_tokens_meta,
+                apply_router_weight_on_input,
+            )
+            return
+
+        assert self.w1_scale is not None and self.w2_scale is not None
+        # The kernel maps global ids through expert_map itself and skips slots
+        # whose local expert is outside [0, E), which is where expert_map
+        # sends experts owned by other ranks (-1).
+        ops.moe_w4a8_decode_rdna3(
+            output,
+            hidden_states,
+            topk_ids.contiguous(),
+            topk_weights.contiguous(),
+            expert_map,
+            workspace2.view(-1).view(torch.uint8),
+            w1,
+            self.w1_scale,
+            self.w1_zp,
+            w2,
+            self.w2_scale,
+            self.w2_zp,
+        )

     - You only need to do this for layers which are not present on all pipeline stages
     - vLLM assumes that there will be only one `nn.ModuleList`, which is distributed across the pipeline stages

@@ -38,23 +38,13 @@ def get_decode_stream_seed(
     prompt_token_ids: list[int] | None,
     skip_special_tokens: bool,
 ) -> list[int] | None:
-    """Return the prompt suffix used to prime a `DecodeStream`.
-
-    `DecodeStream` decodes all of its seed ids on the first `step()`, so
-    seeding it with the whole prompt costs O(prompt) time. Once it has emitted
-    text it keeps only the ids that follow, so the seed only shapes the first
-    delta, and a tail reproduces that delta exactly if:
-
-    - It holds `INITIAL_INCREMENTAL_DETOKENIZATION_OFFSET` tokens that decode
-      to text on their own. Metaspace, WordPiece and leading-`Strip` decoders
-      treat the start of the decoded text specially (e.g. drop a leading
-      space), so tokens that decode to nothing, such as skipped special
-      tokens or whitespace that such a decoder strips, must not count.
-    - Its text does not end in U+FFFD, i.e. it does not start inside the
-      multi-byte character or byte-fallback run that the prompt ends with;
-      such a window is extended to the start of the character. If the prompt
-      itself ends in U+FFFD, `DecodeStream` streams its whole seed text in
-      the first delta, so the full prompt is used to keep that output.
+    """Return a prompt tail that primes a `DecodeStream` like the full prompt.
+
+    The seed only shapes the first delta, so a short tail avoids an O(prompt)
+    decode. The tail holds `INITIAL_INCREMENTAL_DETOKENIZATION_OFFSET` tokens
+    that decode to text on their own (decoders like Metaspace treat the start
+    of the text specially), extended if its text ends in U+FFFD. Falls back to
+    the full prompt if the prompt's own text ends in U+FFFD.
     """
     if not prompt_token_ids:
         return prompt_token_ids

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Which MiniMax-M3 monokernels `--monokernel` may run.
+
+By default every one that fits the deployment. `additional_config` can narrow
+that, e.g. `--additional-config '{"minimax_m3_monokernel": ["drafter"]}'`.
+"""
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+KEY = "minimax_m3_monokernel"
+DECODE = "decode"  # the whole-layer mono decode, else the FFN-only decode
+DRAFTER = "drafter"  # the DSpark drafter kernels
+ALL = frozenset((DECODE, DRAFTER))
+
+
+def enabled_monokernels(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> frozenset[str]:
+    extra = vllm_config.additional_config
+    names = extra.get(KEY) if isinstance(extra, dict) else None
+    if names is None:
+        return ALL
+    selected = frozenset([names] if isinstance(names, str) else names)
+    if not selected or not selected <= ALL:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"additional_config[{KEY!r}] must name one or more of {sorted(ALL)}, "
+            f"got {names!r}"
+        )
+    return selected

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Weight-layout contracts of the gfx1250 W4A4 MoE preshuffled path, checked
+on CPU without launching a kernel:
+
+- the oracle interleaves SILU gate/up rows as [g0, u0, g1, u1, ...], the order
+  the fused swiglu epilogue reads;
+- process_weights_after_loading shuffles the [E, K/2, N] views into a decode
+  view whose last dim is N // 16 (the kernel launcher multiplies it back by 16).
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+pytest.importorskip("aiter.ops.shuffle")
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.aiter_mxfp4_w4a4_moe import (  # noqa: E402
+    AiterW4A4ExpertsMonolithic,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.mxfp4 import (  # noqa: E402
+    _interleave_gate_up_rows,
+)
+
+
+def test_interleave_gate_up_rows_order():
+    num_experts, n, inner = 2, 4, 3
+    gate = torch.arange(num_experts * n * inner).view(num_experts, n, inner)
+    up = gate + 1000
+    out = _interleave_gate_up_rows(torch.cat([gate, up], dim=1))
+    assert out.shape == (num_experts, 2 * n, inner)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out[:, 0::2], gate)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out[:, 1::2], up)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("n", "k_half"), [(512, 256), (1536, 2048)])
+def test_preshuffled_weight_view_restores_n_with_times_16(n, k_half):
+    num_experts = 2
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    for name in ("w13_weight", "w2_weight"):
+        storage = torch.randint(0, 256, (num_experts, n, k_half), dtype=torch.uint8)
+        # The oracle hands over [E, K/2, N] views of [E, N, K/2] storage.
+        layer.register_parameter(
+            name, torch.nn.Parameter(storage.transpose(1, 2), requires_grad=False)
+        )
+    originals = {name: getattr(layer, name).data.clone() for name in ("w13_weight",)}
+
+    experts = AiterW4A4ExpertsMonolithic.__new__(AiterW4A4ExpertsMonolithic)
+    experts.preshuffle_weights = True
+    experts.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+    for name in ("w13_weight", "w2_weight"):

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Run one of a model's real device helpers on the GPU, one row per lane.
+
+The FlyDSL half of the primitive tier (T1) of #68016. T1 is a debugging aid,
+not the numerical contract; the contract is `DecodeNumerics` (T2), which
+compares a decode at its public entry point and holds however the kernel is
+written.
+
+Nothing here computes anything. `run` builds a map kernel whose thread i calls
+the helper under test on row i of the inputs and stores what it returns, so the
+arithmetic under test is the model's own and never a re-implementation of it.
+What it is compared against is `reference.py`; the inputs that make a rounding
+rule observable, and the comparison itself, are in `inputs.py`.
+
+The split is by what the code does, not by what it is written in: this file is
+the only one that needs FlyDSL, and `reference.py` and `inputs.py` are plain
+torch. A model whose helpers are not FlyDSL device functions a test kernel can
+call -- one whose kernels emit their instructions inline, say -- cannot be
+checked at this tier at all, and relies on T2 plus a stage-level check instead.
+It can still use the other two files.
+
+See `tests/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono/test_primitives.py` for a caller.
+"""
+
+import hashlib
+import importlib
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from functools import cache
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import flydsl.compiler as flyc
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+import torch
+from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import buffer_ops as bo
+from flydsl.expr import range_constexpr
+from flydsl.expr.typing import Constexpr, Int64, T
+
+from tests.models.common.specialized_decode.inputs import DEV, F32, I32
+
+# A FlyDSL device function. It takes and returns FlyDSL expressions rather than
+# tensors, so there is nothing more precise to say about it than "callable".
+DeviceFn = Callable[..., Any]
+
+_BLOCK = 256
+
+
+def _rsrc(pointer: Any) -> Any:
+    return bo.create_buffer_resource_from_addr(pointer)
+
+
+def _load_words(src: Any, at: Any, n: int) -> list[Any]:
+    """`n` Int32 at word `at` of `src`, in loads of up to 4 words."""
+    out: list = []
+    while len(out) < n:
+        w = min(4, n - len(out))
+        v = bo.buffer_load(_rsrc(src), at + len(out), vec_width=w, dtype=T.i32)
+        out += [fx.Int32(v)] if w == 1 else [fx.Vector(v)[j] for j in range(w)]
+    return [fx.Int32(x) for x in out]
+
+
+@cache
+def _sources_digest(package: str) -> str:
+    """Of every file of `package`: FlyDSL's compile cache keys a kernel on
+    the sources of its own directory only, not on the helpers it calls, so a
+    test kernel would otherwise keep running against a stale helper."""
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    root = Path(importlib.import_module(package).__file__).parent
+    for f in sorted(root.rglob("*.py")):
+        h.update(f.read_bytes())
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def _map_kernel(key: str, fn: DeviceFn, n_in: int, n_out: int) -> Any:
+    """A kernel whose thread i calls `fn` on words i n_in .. of `src`
+    (Int32) and stores the n_out Int32 it returns at i n_out .. of `dst`.
+    A wave is lanes 64 j .. 64 j + 63 of the rows.
+
+    Deliberately not memoised. `fn` is a fresh closure at every call site, so
+    a cache on it could never hit; FlyDSL's own cache, keyed on the kernel
+    name and `sources`, is what stops a recompile.
+    """
+
+    @flyc.kernel(name=f"mono_prim_{key}", known_block_size=[_BLOCK, 1, 1])
+    def kern(src: Int64, dst: Int64):
+        i = fx.block_idx.x * _BLOCK + fx.thread_idx.x
+        outs = fn(*_load_words(src, i * n_in, n_in))
+        for j in range_constexpr(n_out):
+            bo.buffer_store(fx.Int32(outs[j]), _rsrc(dst), i * n_out + j)
+
+    @flyc.jit
+    def launch(src: Int64, dst: Int64, grid: fx.Int32, sources: Constexpr[str]):
+        kern(src, dst).launch(grid=(grid,), block=(_BLOCK,))
+
+    return launch
+
+
+def run(
+    key: str,
+    fn: DeviceFn,
+    n_out: int,
+    *cols: torch.Tensor,
+    package: str,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """`fn` -- a device helper -- over the rows of the int32 / float32
+    columns `cols`, on the GPU, one row per lane -> int32 [rows, n_out].
+
+    `key` has to be distinct per call site: it names the kernel, and FlyDSL
+    caches on that name and `package`'s digest, so two call sites sharing a
+    key would both get whichever kernel compiled first and the second would
+    quietly assert against the first one's helper. `package` is the model
+    package the helper comes from (see `_sources_digest`).
+    """
+    rows = len(cols[0])
+    assert all(len(c) == rows for c in cols), (
+        f"every column needs the same number of rows, got {[len(c) for c in cols]}"
+    )
+    src = torch.cat(
+        [(c.view(I32) if c.dtype == F32 else c).view(rows, -1) for c in cols], 1
+    )
+    pad = -rows % _BLOCK
+    src = torch.cat([src, src[:1].expand(pad, -1)]).contiguous().to(DEV)
+    dst = torch.zeros(src.shape[0], n_out, dtype=I32, device=DEV)
+    _map_kernel(key, fn, src.shape[1], n_out)(
+        src.data_ptr(), dst.data_ptr(), src.shape[0] // _BLOCK, _sources_digest(package)
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return dst[:rows]
+
+
+def f32(word: Any) -> Any:
+    """An Int32 expression as the Float32 of the same bits."""
+    return fx.Int32(word).bitcast(fx.Float32)
+
+
+def i32(value: Any) -> Any:
+    """A Float32 expression as the Int32 of the same bits."""
+    return fx.Float32(value).bitcast(fx.Int32)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Inputs that make a rounding rule observable, and the comparison of what
+comes back. Plain torch, no device code.
+
+A rounding, a packing or a scale code is only wrong somewhere: at a tie, at a
+subnormal, at the overflow edge, at the value whose quotient by the format
+maximum is a power of two. Random inputs miss all of those, so the generators
+here enumerate them, and the random draws are there to catch what the
+enumeration forgot rather than the other way round.
+
+The float64 definitions these are checked against are in `reference.py`. The
+device side, which is the only part that needs FlyDSL, is in `harness.py`.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+import torch
+
+from tests.models.common.specialized_decode import reference as R
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+# "cuda" on ROCm too, since torch-hip keeps the name. Asked of the platform
+# rather than hardcoded so these run wherever the test does; `or` because an
+# unspecified platform's device_type is "", which torch rejects.
+DEV = current_platform.device_type or "cpu"
+F32, I32 = torch.float32, torch.int32
+
+
+def bits(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """`x` as float32, as its int32 bit patterns, so that a comparison sees a
+    signed zero and distinguishes one ulp rather than printing two equal
+    decimals."""
+    return x.float().view(I32)
+
+
+def _gen(seed: int) -> torch.Generator:
+    return torch.Generator(device=DEV).manual_seed(seed)
+
+
+def _log_uniform(
+    n: int, lo: float, hi: float, g: torch.Generator, signed: bool = True
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """`n` float32 with exponents uniform on [lo, hi], so every binade is
+    sampled equally rather than the top one taking almost every draw."""
+    x = torch.exp2(torch.empty(n, dtype=torch.float64, device=DEV).uniform_(
+        lo, hi, generator=g))  # fmt: skip
+    if signed:
+        x = x * (torch.randint(0, 2, (n,), device=DEV, generator=g) * 2 - 1)
+    return x.float()
+
+
+def edge_floats() -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Every f32 exponent field with the mantissas next to the code / rounding
+    boundaries, positive."""
+    mant = torch.tensor(
+        [0, 1, 2, 0x200000, 0x3FFFFF, 0x400000, 0x400001, 0x7FFFFE, 0x7FFFFF]
+    )
+    bit_patterns = (torch.arange(255)[:, None] << 23) | mant
+    return bit_patterns.flatten().to(I32).view(F32).to(DEV)
+
+
+def neighbours(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """`x` (float32) and its f32 neighbours."""
+    inf = torch.full_like(x, math.inf)
+    return torch.cat([torch.nextafter(x, -inf), x, torch.nextafter(x, inf)])
+
+
+def fp8_bytes(fnuz: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Every E4M3 byte that is not a NaN."""
+    b = torch.arange(256, device=DEV)
+    nan = b == 0x80 if fnuz else (b & 0x7F) == 0x7F
+    return b[~nan].to(torch.uint8)
+
+
+def fp8_domain(fnuz: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Every E4M3 magnitude and every midpoint between neighbours, each with
+    its f32 neighbours, both signs; past the range up to inf; 2^20 random."""
+    fp8_dtype = torch.float8_e4m3fnuz if fnuz else torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    codes = torch.arange(0, 127, dtype=torch.uint8).view(fp8_dtype)
+    magnitudes = codes.double().to(DEV)
+    midpoints = (magnitudes[1:] + magnitudes[:-1]) / 2
+    past_max = torch.tensor([464.0, 480, 1e6, 3e38], device=DEV)
+    values = neighbours(torch.cat([magnitudes, midpoints, past_max]).float())
+    random_values = _log_uniform(1 << 20, -14, 10, _gen(0))
+    infinities = torch.tensor([math.inf, -math.inf], device=DEV)
+    values = torch.cat([values, -values, random_values, infinities])
+    return torch.cat([values, values.new_tensor([1e-40, -1e-40])])
+
+
+def all_byte_words(exclude: tuple[int, ...] = ()) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Words covering every allowed byte value in every byte position, with
+    random other bytes."""
+    b = torch.tensor([v for v in range(256) if v not in exclude], device=DEV)
+    allowed = b.to(torch.uint8)
+    g = _gen(10)
+    words = []
+    for pos in range(4):
+        w = allowed[torch.randint(0, len(b), (len(b), 4), device=DEV, generator=g)]
+        w[:, pos] = allowed
+        words.append(w)
+    return torch.cat(words).contiguous().view(I32).flatten()
+
+
+def e2m1_bytes(codes: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """E2M1 values of the 8 nibbles of int32 words, low nibble first."""
+    nib = (codes.long()[:, None] >> (4 * torch.arange(8, device=DEV))) & 0xF
+    return R.E2M1_VALUES.to(DEV)[nib]
+
+
+def assert_bit_exact(
+    actual: torch.Tensor,
+    expected: torch.Tensor,
+    helper: str,
+    sent: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """`actual == expected` row for row, naming the helper and the first rows
+    that differ.
+
+    `sent` is what was fed to the helper, one row per row of `actual`. Plain
+    `torch.equal` is enough where the input is a handful of values and is used
+    directly there; the generators above run to a million rows, and a bare
+    `False` over a million roundings says nothing about which one broke.
+    """
+    # Not just a sanity check: `!=` would broadcast a mismatch into a square
+    # of comparisons and the report below would then be about rows that were
+    # never computed.
+    assert actual.shape == expected.shape, (
+        f"{helper}: got shape {tuple(actual.shape)}, want {tuple(expected.shape)}"
+    )
+    differs = actual != expected
+    if actual.is_floating_point():
+        # -0.0 == +0.0, so a dropped zero sign would pass on `!=` alone, and
+        # OCP's 0x80 is a negative zero that `fp8_bytes` feeds in.
+        differs |= torch.signbit(actual) != torch.signbit(expected)
+    bad = differs.view(len(expected), -1).any(1).nonzero().flatten()[:3]
+    assert bad.numel() == 0, (
+        f"{helper} differs at {sent[bad].tolist()}: "
+        f"got {actual[bad].tolist()}, want {expected[bad].tolist()}"
+    )

+class SlicedQKVAttention(nn.Module):
+    """Phi3-style: one packed projection sliced into q/k/v in the forward."""
+
+    is_causal = True
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        hidden: int = 32,
+        head_dim: int = 8,
+        heads: int = 4,
+        kv_heads: int = 1,
+        layer_idx: int = 0,
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.config = SimpleNamespace(_attn_implementation="vllm")
+        self.layer_idx = layer_idx
+        self.head_dim = head_dim
+        self.scaling = head_dim**-0.5
+        self.query_pos = heads * head_dim
+        self.kv_dim = kv_heads * head_dim
+        self.qkv_proj = nn.Linear(hidden, self.query_pos + 2 * self.kv_dim, bias=False)
+        self.o_proj = nn.Linear(self.query_pos, hidden, bias=False)
+
+    def attend(self, hidden_states, q, k, v, attention_mask, **kwargs):
+        from transformers.modeling_utils import ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS
+
+        input_shape = hidden_states.shape[:-1]
+        q = q.reshape(*input_shape, -1, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
+        k, v = k.unsqueeze(1), v.unsqueeze(1)
+        attention_interface = ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS.get_interface(
+            self.config._attn_implementation, None
+        )
+        attn_output, attn_weights = attention_interface(
+            self, q, k, v, attention_mask, scaling=self.scaling, **kwargs
+        )
+        return self.o_proj(attn_output.reshape(*input_shape, -1)), attn_weights
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, attention_mask=None, **kwargs):
+        qkv = self.qkv_proj(hidden_states)
+        query_pos = self.query_pos
+        q = qkv[..., :query_pos]
+        k = qkv[..., query_pos : query_pos + self.kv_dim]
+        v = qkv[..., query_pos + self.kv_dim :]
+        return self.attend(hidden_states, q, k, v, attention_mask, **kwargs)
+
+
+class RopeSlicedQKVAttention(SlicedQKVAttention):
+    """Also slices a tensor derived from the projection with int bounds."""
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, attention_mask=None, **kwargs):
+        qkv = self.qkv_proj(hidden_states)
+        query_pos = self.query_pos
+        q = qkv[..., :query_pos]
+        k = qkv[..., query_pos : query_pos + self.kv_dim]
+        v = qkv[..., query_pos + self.kv_dim :]
+        q = torch.cat([q[..., :4] * 2, q[..., 4:]], dim=-1)
+        return self.attend(hidden_states, q, k, v, attention_mask, **kwargs)
+
+
+class GapSlicedQKVAttention(SlicedQKVAttention):
+    """A hole between k and v, so the slices do not tile the projection."""
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, attention_mask=None, **kwargs):
+        qkv = self.qkv_proj(hidden_states)
+        query_pos = self.query_pos
+        q = qkv[..., :query_pos]
+        k = qkv[..., query_pos : query_pos + self.kv_dim]
+        v = qkv[..., query_pos + self.kv_dim + 1 :]
+        return self.attend(hidden_states, q, k, v, attention_mask, **kwargs)
+
+
+class TracedBoundSlicedQKVAttention(SlicedQKVAttention):
+    """Slice bounds computed from a tensor shape, so fx sees them as nodes."""
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, attention_mask=None, **kwargs):
+        qkv = self.qkv_proj(hidden_states)
+        n = hidden_states.shape[-1]
+        k_end = n + self.kv_dim
+        q = qkv[..., :n]
+        k = qkv[..., n:k_end]
+        v = qkv[..., k_end:]
+        return self.attend(hidden_states, q, k, v, attention_mask, **kwargs)
+
+
+class AnnotatedSlicedQKVAttention(SlicedQKVAttention):
+    """The source binds the projection with an annotated assign."""
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, attention_mask=None, **kwargs):
+        qkv: torch.Tensor = self.qkv_proj(hidden_states)
+        query_pos = self.query_pos
+        q = qkv[..., :query_pos]
+        k = qkv[..., query_pos : query_pos + self.kv_dim]
+        v = qkv[..., query_pos + self.kv_dim :]
+        return self.attend(hidden_states, q, k, v, attention_mask, **kwargs)
+
+
+class ReusedSlicedQKVAttention(SlicedQKVAttention):
+    """The projection has a fourth consumer."""
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, attention_mask=None, **kwargs):
+        qkv = self.qkv_proj(hidden_states)
+        query_pos = self.query_pos
+        q = qkv[..., :query_pos] + qkv[..., :query_pos]
+        k = qkv[..., query_pos : query_pos + self.kv_dim]
+        v = qkv[..., query_pos + self.kv_dim :]
+        return self.attend(hidden_states, q, k, v, attention_mask, **kwargs)
+
